title: Pris, mis, ouvert, offert et voulu
summary: Retrieve useful irregular participles and keep derivative verbs in their families.
objectives: Use `prendre` and `mettre` families in the `passé composé`.

sources.label: Public A2 index: topic-coverage reference only

sections.title: Families of short participles
paragraphs: A past participle is the second verb part after the auxiliary. `Prendre` becomes `pris`, not `prendu`. `Apprendre` (learn), `comprendre` (understand), `reprendre` (take again/resume) and `surprendre` (surprise) give `appris`, `compris`, `repris` and `surpris`. `Mettre` becomes `mis`; `remettre` (put back/hand in), `permettre` (allow), `promettre` (promise) and `admettre` (admit) give `remis`, `permis`, `promis` and `admis`.
points: Use the full `avoir` pattern with each participle: `j'ai pris, tu as pris, il/elle/on a pris, nous avons pris, vous avez pris, ils/elles ont pris`. Replace `pris` with `mis`, `appris`, `compris`, `remis`, etc.
The final `s` belongs to the participle itself. It is not a plural marker in `j'ai pris`.

examples.french: Vous **avez remis** les clés à l'accueil.
examples.english: You handed the keys in at reception.

sections.title: The present pattern does not predict the participle
paragraphs: `Ouvrir` uses `ouvert`; `découvrir` and `recouvrir` give `découvert` and `recouvert`. `Offrir` gives `offert` and `souffrir` gives `souffert`. Their present forms resemble `-er` verbs, but their participles do not end in `-é`. `Vouloir` gives `voulu`. `J'ai voulu` can describe a specific wish or attempt; it does not by itself guarantee success. `Je n'ai pas voulu` often means 'I refused/did not want to' in a particular situation.
points: All take `avoir`: `j'ai ouvert, tu as ouvert, il/elle/on a ouvert, nous avons ouvert, vous avez ouvert, ils/elles ont ouvert`. Substitute `découvert`, `offert`, `souffert` or `voulu`.
No subject agreement in these `avoir` examples: `elles ont offert`, not `elles ont offertes`, when the object follows.

examples.french: Ils **ont ouvert** le centre en mai.
examples.english: They opened the centre in May.

examples.french: Tu **as découvert** une nouvelle piste cyclable.
examples.english: You discovered a new cycle path.

examples.french: Nous **avons offert** notre aide, mais elle **a souffert** du manque de matériel.
examples.english: We offered our help, but she suffered from the lack of equipment.

examples.french: J'**ai voulu** réparer la lampe, mais je n'ai pas réussi.
examples.english: I wanted to repair the lamp, but I did not succeed.
examples.note: `Voulu` does not assert successful completion of the repair.

mistakes.why: For `ouvrir`, the participle is `ouvert`; `ouvrer` is a different, uncommon verb.

practice.prompt: Passé composé of prendre: Vous ___ rendez-vous.
Passé composé of mettre: Elle ___ son manteau.
Passé composé of ouvrir: Nous ___ la porte.
Passé composé of vouloir: Tu ___ essayer.
Passé composé of apprendre: Ils ___ la nouvelle hier.
Passé composé of comprendre: J'___ votre demande.
Passé composé of permettre: Ce bus ___ un trajet direct.
Passé composé of promettre: Nous ___ de venir.
Passé composé of découvrir: Vous ___ une erreur.
Passé composé of offrir: Elles ___ des fleurs.
practice.explanation: Offert has no subject agreement here.

practice.prompt: Passé composé of souffrir: Il ___ de la chaleur.
Supply vouloir in the passé composé: Elle n'___ répondre.
practice.explanation: The negative wraps the auxiliary: n'a pas voulu.

practice.prompt: Passé composé of reprendre: Tu ___ le travail.
Passé composé of remettre: J'___ le dossier au responsable.
Passé composé of recouvrir: La neige ___ la route.
Passé composé of admettre: Ils ___ leur erreur.

production_task.prompt: Explain how you tried to solve a problem at work. Include what you learned, what you did and an offer of help.
production_task.model_answer: J'ai appris qu'une porte était bloquée. J'ai pris la clé de secours et j'ai ouvert la porte. Une collègue a offert son aide. Nous avons remis la clé à sa place.
production_task.translation: I learned that a door was blocked. I took the spare key and opened the door. A colleague offered her help. We put the key back in its place.
rubric: Explain the result, not just a list of verbs.
